background_notes.fact: For a complex-linear endomorphism T of V and an additive subgroup M of V with T(M) contained in M, the restriction T|_M is an endomorphism of the induced integer module M. This applies to x,y,h and every X_r,Y_r here.

grounds.reason: V is a complex vector space; x,y,h are complex-linear endomorphisms; M is an additive subgroup with its induced integer-module structure.
Each X_r is a complex scalar multiple of a power of the complex-linear x, hence is complex-linear.
Each Y_r is a complex scalar multiple of a power of the complex-linear y, hence is complex-linear.
F001 establishes preservation of M by x,y and every X_r,Y_r.
Before the restriction step, S002 establishes preservation of M by h using H002 and subgroup closure.

background_notes.justification: Complex linearity gives additivity. Additivity implies T(0)=0 and T(-m)=-T(m); repeated addition gives T(nm)=nT(m) for natural n, and the negative case gives the identity for all integers. Preservation makes these identities identities in M, proving integer-linearity of the restriction.
